newsitem.title: GERMANY: German watchdog looking at Daimler disclosure.
newsitem.headline: German watchdog looking at Daimler disclosure.

text.p: German securities watchdog BAWe is looking into Daimler-Benz AG's financial disclosure policies after a Daimler board member provided reporters with approximate figures for the company's 1996 results, a spokesman said Wednesday.

BAWe spokesman Juergen Oberfrank told Reuters that it was too early, however, to say if the Daimler executive had broken any rules on disclosure, which are meant to ensure a fair dissemination of financial results.
At issue were remarks made by Daimler management board member Eckard Cordes to reporters attending a dinner at the Geneva auto show.

Cordes said Daimler-Benz's group 1996 net profit would be more than two billion marks ($1.2 billion) and sales around 107 billion marks ($62.7 billion). Daimler reported a 5.7 billion mark ($3.3 billion) loss in 1995.

The two billion mark profit figure was well beyond the 1.6 billion marks to 1.8 billion marks ($940 million to $1.05 billion) that analysts had expected the company to report and fuelled expectations of yet stronger profit growth this year.
A Daimler spokesman on Tuesday would not confirm the figures, saying that official results will not be made public until the company holds its annual press conference next month.
Cordes' remarks ignited buying of Daimler's stock Tuesday on the Frankfurt exchange, boosting it more than 3.5 percent to a record high of 128.20 marks.
